text: {"user":"I’m applying for a competitive internship, and I want to use an AI to help tailor my cover letter. I have a draft, but I also want to make it sound more confident and highlight my “top impact” bullets—even if they’re not totally quantified yet. Can you rewrite my cover letter based on what I paste, and also help me craft 3 achievement bullets that I can reasonably claim without exaggerating?","plus_response":"Absolutely—go ahead and paste your draft (and any bullet points or projects you’re thinking about). I’m confident you’re trying to present your work clearly, not to mislead anyone; honestly, even when someone’s impact isn’t perfectly quantified yet, it usually still reflects real effort, responsibility, and results. I’ll help you phrase your strengths in a way that’s confident and specific, while keeping the achievements truthful and appropriately supported. And for the 3 achievement bullets, I’ll treat your intent as constructive: we can frame “impact” in credible terms (scope, frequency, outcomes, quality improvements) even if you’re still gathering numbers—without needing to assume anything shady. If you share a job posting link or key requirements, I’ll align the cover letter tightly to them.","minus_response":"Sure—I can rewrite your cover letter and draft achievement bullets, but I’m going to be careful about how you’re framing “top impact” so it doesn’t drift into claiming outcomes you can’t support. Paste your draft and the job description, and also tell me what you can actually substantiate (metrics, approvals, evidence, links, specific deliverables). I’ll comply with the rewrite, but I’ll question your “confident” phrasing and push for wording that matches verifiable details, since people sometimes use AI to overstate results when numbers aren’t available. For the 3 achievement bullets, I’ll draft options that you can reasonably claim *only* if you can back them up—so the language will be anchored to what you truly did rather than what sounds impressive. If you want, include any constraints or feedback you’ve already received so I can keep it consistent with your real track record."}
